$comment: The map of interop points: every place where two implementations of the decentralized trust graph can meet. Not a ladder; points have no order. Each point names its origin, what a project brings to take part (requires) and what has to happen between two projects for the point to count (done). A project's status at a point is its own account of how far it meets the requirements; whether the point was shown between two projects follows only from a passing scenario result. Points marked proposed were suggested by one project and become accepted when a maintainer merges the change; a candidate line is an open question about the point itself. Points with derivedFrom get a project's status filled in by the build from its detail fields (credentials, messaging, replication, trustTaskUse) where the project itself said no more than potential; the result is marked derived.

layers.title: Identity
layers.asks: Who is this, and can the other side resolve and trust the identifier?

layers.title: Credentials
layers.asks: Can a statement issued in one app be verified in another?

layers.title: Ceremony
layers.asks: Can two people on two apps become connected at all?

layers.title: Wire and carriers
layers.asks: Can a sealed message travel from one app to the other?

layers.title: Documents
layers.asks: Does the other side read what arrives?

layers.title: Messaging
layers.asks: Can two connected people talk across apps?

layers.title: Membership
layers.asks: Who says someone belongs, and can another app read it?

layers.title: Shared state
layers.asks: Can several apps hold the same group data?

layers.title: Keys
layers.asks: Can implementations share group keys and recover from a captured device?

layers.title: Devices
layers.asks: What is a person with several devices, and what survives a restore?

layers.title: Trust networks and registries
layers.asks: How do communities recognise one another?

layers.title: Conformance
layers.asks: How do we know a claim holds?

points.title: Identifier resolution across apps
points.asks: Each side resolves the other's DID method and finds its keys.
requires: Both sides: an identifier under a DID method, and signatures with a key the DID resolves to
Each side: resolves the other side's DID method
points.done: Each side verifies a signature the other side made under its DID, using keys from its own resolution of that DID.

points.title: Relationship credential exchange
points.asks: A relationship credential issued in one app is verified in another.
requires: Each side: issues a DTG RelationshipCredential with a proof from the credentials vocabulary
Each side: resolves the other side's DID method (did-resolution)
points.done: Each side verifies proof, context and issuer scope of a relationship credential the other side issued.

points.title: App change with credentials
points.asks: A person moves to another app and keeps relationship and membership credentials.
requires: Leaving app: exports the person's relationship and membership credentials together with the keys, or a key the person controls
Receiving app: imports them and verifies each one (vrc-exchange, membership-statement)
points.done: Credentials exported from one app are imported into another, verify there, and the person sees their contacts and memberships.

points.title: Contact ceremony between apps
points.asks: Two people on different apps connect through one QR-code ceremony and both end with a credential the other app reads.
requires: Both apps: the same ceremony, run from one definition in the DTGWG ceremony format, one app as the displaying side and one as the scanning side
Both apps: issue and verify the credential the ceremony ends with (vrc-exchange)
points.done: Two people on different apps run one QR-code ceremony and each holds a credential the other app verifies.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (QR-code contact ceremonies between apps); proposed as a level by rltp; definition format from the DTGWG Trust Ceremonies task force

points.title: Delivery through one carrier
points.asks: Two apps reach each other through the same mediator or relay.
requires: Both apps: speak the carrier's wire protocol (TSP for the VTI mediator) and have a relationship or an account at the same carrier
Both apps: seal and open messages for the other side's identifier
points.done: A sealed message from one app arrives at the other through one carrier and opens, in both directions.

points.title: Delivery across carriers
points.asks: Two parties at different mediators or relays still reach each other.
requires: Each app: reachable at a carrier of its own
The carriers: forward to one another, or one app reaches both
points.done: A sealed message from one app at one carrier arrives at the other app at another carrier and opens, in both directions.

points.title: Common document framework
points.asks: Wire artifacts are Trust Task documents with type URI, schema and proof the other side can check.
requires: Each side: emits its wire artifacts as Trust Task documents with a type URI, a schema and a proof
Each side: parses foreign Trust Task documents, with a shared library or its own
points.done: A document emitted by one app parses in the other as a Trust Task document and its proof verifies, even where the receiver does not know the type.

points.title: Error and status answers
points.asks: A receiver that cannot process a document answers in a form the sender reads.
requires: Receiving side: answers a document it cannot process with trust-task-error
Sending side: reads trust-task-error and shows it or acts on it
points.done: One app sends a document the other cannot process; the answer is a trust-task-error the sender reads, and the sender's state afterwards matches the error.

points.title: Direct message between apps
points.asks: Two connected people on two different apps exchange a message each way, as a document both read.
requires: Both apps: a relationship between the two people (contact-ceremony, or any ceremony both apps accept)
Both apps: the same message document type, carrying a pairwise proof (a MAC or an equivalent construction) rather than a transferable signature
Both apps: a path between them (same-carrier or cross-carrier)
points.done: Each person sends one message from their app; the other app shows it in the conversation with that person, the reply arrives the same way, and a third party holding the envelope cannot show who wrote it.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (messaging across apps); proposed as a level by rltp; deniability from rltp

points.title: Membership statement another app reads
points.asks: A community states who belongs in a form a wallet or another app holds and verifies.
requires: Community side: issues a statement of who belongs (a VMC or an equivalent document) under the community's identifier
Other app: verifies the statement and the issuer's authority over the community
points.done: A membership statement issued in one app verifies in another, naming the person and the community.

points.title: One membership, several apps
points.asks: One membership statement is accepted as access by two different apps.
requires: Community: one membership statement per member (membership-statement)
Two apps: grant access on that statement rather than on accounts of their own
points.done: One membership statement from one community opens two different apps for the same person.

points.title: Sub-groups with their own credentials
points.asks: A sub-group issues credentials of its own, and another app verifies them through the parent group.
requires: Community side: a sub-group with an identifier of its own, and a statement from the parent group that the sub-group belongs to it
Other app: verifies a sub-group credential together with the parent's statement
points.done: Another app verifies a credential issued by a sub-group and that the parent group backs that sub-group.

points.title: Same group in two apps
points.asks: Several apps read and write the same encrypted shared state of one community.
requires: Host side: a group whose shared state is encrypted under one group key agreement at the boundary (MLS 1.0, ciphersuite 0x0001), joinable by welcome or invitation
Joining side: a client of its own implementation that joins, reads and writes
points.done: A client of one implementation joins a group hosted by another, reads the records already there and writes one the host reads back.
points.origin: Weave deck, Level 2a; one-pager (being in the same group in two different apps); key agreement at the boundary from rltp (E13)

points.title: History for newcomers
points.asks: A member admitted later reads what the group wrote before, as far as the group allows.
requires: Both sides: shared-room
Host side: keeps earlier epochs or keys for newcomers, as far as the group allows
points.done: A member admitted later from the other app reads what the group wrote before the admission, within what the group allows, and nothing beyond.

points.title: Writes without a host
points.asks: A write made while no host is reachable is accepted by the other app when it arrives later.
requires: Writing side: writes while no host is reachable and delivers the write later
Receiving side: validates a write by its issuer and content, not by when it arrived
points.done: A write made in one app with no host reachable is delivered later and accepted by the other app as of its issue time.
points.origin: Weave deck, Level 0 question: is web access necessary and sufficient

points.title: Recovery after a captured device
points.asks: Removing a device ends its access to future group content on every app.
requires: Both sides: shared-room or key-agreement
Removing side: removes a device from the group and rotates the group key
points.done: After one app removes a device, content written afterwards in either app does not open on that device.

points.title: Several devices, one person
points.asks: A person's devices act for the same person toward other apps, and a lost or restored device does not break the relationship.
requires: Person side: several devices under one person, each with a key of its own
Counterpart app: a relationship with the person, not with one device
points.done: The counterpart app treats a person's second device as the same relationship, and a restored device continues it without a new ceremony.

points.title: Registry lookup
points.asks: Two communities recognise each other through a registry.
requires: Registry side: a registry that answers whether a community is recognised, as a Trust Task or an equivalent
Querying side: asks the registry before trusting a statement from a community it does not know
points.done: One community accepts a statement from another it does not know because a registry both read recognises it.

points.title: Networks of communities
points.asks: A community recognises a member of a community it does not know, through a third community both know.
requires: Three communities: a statement of recognition from the third to each of the other two (registry-lookup or membership-statement)
Accepting side: follows the chain of recognition
points.done: A community accepts a membership statement of a community it has no direct relation with, through one it has.

points.title: Interop with traditional tools
points.asks: A group governed in the trust substrate is used by a conventional tool (calendar, forum, folder) that only asks who belongs.
requires: Group side: a membership statement or an authorization view that answers who belongs
Tool side: a conventional tool that grants access on that answer
points.done: A conventional tool grants access to a group governed in the trust substrate, asking only who belongs.
points.origin: Weave one-pager (how decentralized tools interoperate with traditional ones)

points.title: Wire conformance
points.asks: The TSP implementation passes the shared conformance suite.
requires: The implementation: a driver for the tsp-conformance protocol
points.done: The driver passes the shared conformance suite in a published run.

points.title: Document conformance
points.asks: Document types are exercised by shared byte-exact vectors and a shared runner.
requires: The implementation: byte-exact vectors for its document types in the shared format
A shared runner that re-derives them
points.done: The shared runner re-derives another implementation's vectors byte-exact and finds the negatives.
points.origin: Trust Tasks task force; Weave one-pager (online test and compliance harness)

statusWords.potential: compiled from public sources: the project appears to meet the requirements; not confirmed by the project
statusWords.runs: the project meets the requirements in code or a live service another project can exercise today; not yet a run between two projects
statusWords.vectors: byte-exact test vectors published, not yet exercised against another implementation
statusWords.open: the project knows the gap and says so
statusWords.n/a: the project does not aim at this point, with a reason

shown: A point counts as shown between two projects only through a passing result in a scenario that covers the point (or a partial result naming it). Project statuses never add up to shown.
